item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial ends early due to "unforeseen circumstance"
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's trial continued Wednesday in Massachusetts, though testimony for the day ended earlier than expected.

item.title: Sneak peek: The Hit-and-Run Homicide of Davis McClendon
item.description: ENCORE: A romance is cut short when a man is found dead near his mangled car. His newfound love is convinced it was no accident. "48 Hours" correspondent Anne-Marie Green reports Saturday, August 22 at 10/9c on CBS and streaming on Paramount+.

item.title: Biggest wins, losses and upsets in key primary races
item.description: CBS News political director Fin Gómez and congressional correspondent Nikole Killion break down the results of major primary races, from Florida to Alaska.

item.title: 5 Americans among 7 people killed in Kenya helicopter crash
item.description: NBCUniversal said its Florida-based journalist, José Alberto Suárez, was among those killed in the crash.

item.title: Israel orders criminal probe into killing of 5-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza
item.description: Israel says military police will investigate the killing of Hind Rajab, a young girl in Gaza whose death at the hands of its forces drew an international outcry.

item.title: Israel opens criminal probes into killings of Hind Rajab and Gaza rescue workers
item.description: The Israeli military has ordered a criminal investigation into its forces' killing of 5-year-old Hind Rajab, a Palestinian girl whose 2024 death sparked international outrage. CBS News' Ramy Inocencio has more.

item.title: U.S. might return to negotiations "at some point," Trump says
item.description: President Trump said Wednesday the U.S. might return to negotiations with Iran eventually, but said currently "the situation is so good."

item.title: Early details on potential Trump-Kim Jong Un meeting
item.description: President Trump said Wednesday that he expects to meet again with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un this year. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi has more.

item.title: Army unit offers 4-day pass to play Grand Theft Auto as reenlistment incentive
item.description: Eligible soldiers must reenlist for a minimum of two years and up to six years.

item.title: Takeaways from the Florida and Alaska primaries
item.description: Florida and Alaska both held primaries with national implications on Tuesday. CBS News' Zak Hudak and Anthony Salvanto break down what we learned from the results.

item.title: How progressive wins in Democratic primaries are shaping the midterms
item.description: Progressive momentum has been a prominent storyline as Democrats look to flip control of the House and Senate next year. But how far will it go?

item.title: Sculpting Evolution: Using genetic engineering to curb Lyme | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: Lyme disease is rapidly emerging in southern Appalachia, the CDC said in a new report. In 2025, Dr. Jon LaPook, on assignment for 60 Minutes, met a team of scientists on Nantucket who are using genetic engineering to fight the spread of the disease.

item.title: Trump boasts about Kim Jong Un friendship after slamming South Korea
item.description: President Trump took questions from reporters on North Korea, Canadian tariffs, Iran and more. Plus, CBS News' Eleanor Watson has the latest headlines on the war in Iran.

item.title: Darline Graham says she's "not that informed on national security" at debate
item.description: The Republican nominee for the South Carolina Senate seat will be determined in the runoff between Sen. Darline Graham and Rep. Ralph Norman on Aug. 25.

item.title: Moving pillowcase leads to discovery of reptiles in car seized at border
item.description: Federal officers found a moving pillowcase in a car that was seized at the U.S.-Mexico border. A collection of stolen exotic reptiles was inside.

item.title: Moderna stock surges as melanoma vaccine trial shows "landmark moment"
item.description: Moderna and Merck announced study results that reflect a "landmark moment" in treatment for one of the deadliest forms of skin cancer.

item.title: Trump nominates policy aide Dr. Heidi Overton as next FDA commissioner
item.description: President Trump announced he's nominating Dr. Heidi Overton, a deputy assistant to the president for domestic policy, to be the next head of the FDA.

item.title: Texas rancher on Big Bend border wall outcry: "About protecting our land"
item.description: Texans and bipartisan lawmakers are pushing back against a U.S. Customs and Border Protection plan to build a border wall at Big Bend National Park. In reaction, CBP has temporarily paused construction. CBS News' Nicole Sganga has the latest.

item.title: Mexico rejects latest Trump administration crackdown that is leaving migrants in other countries
item.description: Mexico is angry with the Trump administration's move to deport Mexican migrants to other countries, CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez reports.

item.title: Woman describes confronting man in Chucky-style mask who chased her
item.description: Police in Philadelphia are searching for a man they say chased at least a half dozen people last week within a half hour while wearing a Chucky-style mask.

item.title: Bond market sell-off threatens to drive up loan costs
item.description: The yield on the 30-year Treasury this week hit its highest level since 2007, a rise that could put upward pressure on borrowing costs.

item.title: Trump says he expects to meet with North Korea's Kim Jong Un this year
item.description: President Trump wants to meet again with Kim Jong Un to discuss denuclearization, the Wall Street Journal reports, despite having nothing to show for 3 previous summits.

item.title: Wildest campaign moments in Florida's primary elections
item.description: Axios reporter and CBS News contributor Marc Caputo argues that weirdness and misbehavior in Florida's primary elections evoked the "Florida Man" meme.

item.title: The DOJ official behind a record number of federal monitors going to midterm polling sites
item.description: The Department of Justice plans to send out a record 1,000 federal monitors to polling sites across the U.S., a higher number than is usual. CBS News' Sarah Lynch explains what's behind the push.

item.title: Vaccine exemptions hit a record last year, the CDC says. Here's what that means for parents.
item.description: Kindergarten vaccine exemptions hit a record high last year in the U.S., according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data. Dr. Celine Gounder breaks it down.

item.title: H.R. McMaster reacts to Trump apparently pushing for meeting with North Korea's Kim Jong Un
item.description: The U.S. and South Korea will cut short their annual joint military exercises at the behest of President Trump, who is apparently seeking a meeting with North Korean dictator Kim Jong Un, according to a report from The Wall Street Journal. Retired Lt. Gen. H.R. McMaster joins CBS News with his reaction.

item.title: Sen. Dan Sullivan, Mary Peltola advance in Alaska Senate primary
item.description: In Alaska, the top four vote getters in the primary advance to the general election.

item.title: Justice Department to send a record 1,000 monitors to midterm polling places
item.description: The Justice Department is planning to deploy a record 1,000 federal monitors to polling places throughout the U.S. for the midterm elections.

item.title: Activists who posed as Minnesota voters during primary could be in legal trouble
item.description: An undercover video could land a handful of activists in legal trouble. They pretended to be Minnesota voters during the primary.

item.title: School vaccination rates decline again as exemptions reach new high
item.description: U.S. kindergarten vaccination rates have declined again, with exemptions reaching a record high for the 2025-2026 school year
